title: Interactive phases: a plan-declared stop where a person corrects the pattern, with any editor and any agent CLI

ground.note: The first draft, Abandoned on 2026-10-19. This spec keeps its structure and what the 2026-10-19 decisions leave alone: the per-phase `mode`, where lint sits, review-only phases, `awaiting_review`, exit 13, gate first then handoff then commit, the four-section handoff, `## Review corrections` for every later phase, the empty commit when nothing changed, and the reset, adjust-plan and archive rules. It was dropped because its optional seeded session, started interactively by `phax enter-phase`, had an id phax could not learn on codex or vibe. Its ground read (oracle-phases, phase-decision-requests, phaxPlan.ts, planDocument.ts, parsePlanMarkdown.ts, promptGeneration.ts, handoffInjection.ts, handoffGuidance.ts, phaseGuard.ts, resume.ts, resumeInstructions.ts, backend.ts, status.ts, the phax-planning skill) was done the same day, and this spec relies on it.

The 2026-10-18 spike on the archived run phax.brief-provider, stopped after phase-03 of 7. A seeded agent in the stopped worktree saw on its own that the later phases copy phase-03's pattern, and it turned a comment into a fix plus a test. The spike left two questions for this spec: how the phase closes (gates, handoff, commit) and how long the session lives. Its worktree had no node_modules, so the real stop must run the phase setup.

Claude Code's interactive resume is `claude --resume <id>`. A pre-prompted start uses `--session-id <id>`, which is the only way phax can know an interactive session's id up front. `buildDecideInvocation` is Claude-only.

Both interactive resume and a pre-prompted start answer `unsupported` and name `codex exec resume <session-id>` for a manual resume. This spec lifts interactive resume for codex, now that it has been verified.
Both interactive resume and a pre-prompted start answer `unsupported` and name `vibe --resume <session-id>`. Vibe's interactive resume stays unverified.
enter-phase reads the phase's agent binding and runs the adapter's resume invocation. It fails with the adapter's `unsupported` message for codex and mistral-vibe.
The per-phase agent binding: provider, adapter, model, effort, a nullable sessionId, the worktree and a status enum that already contains `awaiting_manual_review`.
RunState: created, running, failed, review_open, completed, stopped, archived, interrupted, rate_limited. PhaseState and the hierarchical PhaxState have no state for waiting on a person.

A phase session runs codex under `sandbox_mode="workspace-write"`, with its writable roots and network access set and approval set to never. Completions run under `sandbox_mode="read-only"`, so codex has a read-only mode phax already uses.

The secure vibe flags are `--workdir` and `--add-dir`, with no per-command or network restriction. The model is passed through the `VIBE_ACTIVE_MODEL` environment variable, and phax uses no read-only mode for vibe.

After decide's interactive session, phax resumes that session headless for a structured answer. A refused answer gets one corrective resume, and each resume's transcript is written to the artifact's folder. Closing an interactive phase follows the same pattern.
EXIT_CODE_MEANINGS runs from 0 to 12, and a test keeps the README table in step with it. 8 (rate or usage limit) and 9 (no changes) are resumable codes, and 13 is free.

The shared run preflight set. `phax run` runs it before it names the run, and executePlan runs it again as the resume re-check, so `phax resume` runs it too. Its `phase-models` check calls `preflightPhaseModels`, the function lint's `models` check calls, and refuses with exit 11, as `phase-sections` does. `phax validate --plan` only decodes `phax-plan.json` and runs none of it.

A plan-document phase's keys run `…, plannedFilesToCreate, plannedFilesToEdit, optionalFilesToEdit, boundaryContracts, …, expectedHandoff, commit, modelReason, model, effort`. A `phax-plan.json` phase ends `…, optionalFilesToEdit, commit`.

Approved. It covers `review-code` and `--new-session`, `review_open`, and `phax run --append`, which takes a run from review_open back to running. The interactive phase sits before all of this and changes none of it.

Draft. Renames the plan document's `modelReason` to `assignmentReason`, rendered as an `**Assignment reason:**` line under the model and effort lines, keeps `assignmentReason`, `model` and `effort` as a phase's last three keys, and holds each phase's model and effort to the owner's bounds in lint and in the run preflight, matching a phase through its create, edit and optional files. This spec ships with it, in one plan-document lift.

context:
phax runs a plan's phases in order. Each phase gets its own worktree on `<run.branch>--phase-NN`, branched off the previous phase's branch. A headless agent session does the work, the gate runs, and a same-session fix loop repairs a red gate. phax then commits the phase and writes its handoff to `<run>/<phase>/phase-handoff.md`, in four sections: What was delivered, Key decisions and why, Exact locations, What the next phase needs to know. The next phase's prompt carries only the immediately previous handoff, under `## Previous phase handoff`. The last phase stays open in `review_open`.

Runs stay autonomous (decided 2026-10-10). A run stops only on a cause a machine detects: a rate or usage limit (exit 8), an exhausted or refused gate (exit 4), a phase with no change (exit 9), or a failed commit or cleanup. Each pause writes `resume-instructions.md`. Resuming after an exhausted gate runs the gate again first, and a green gate commits with no new agent invocation. The `phase-decision-requests` spec, which let an agent stop mid-phase to ask a person, is parked. Inside a phase worktree, which phax recognises by its gitignored `.phax-context/` folder, the phase guard refuses `resume`, `enter-phase`, `shell`, `open`, `run`, `reset-phase` and the artifact transitions. `phax report` opens a GitHub issue from telemetry; it is not a status view. The status views are `phax ls` and `phax session-info`.

Interactive re-entry today is `phax enter-phase <run> <phase>`. For Claude Code it runs `claude --resume <id>`. The codex and mistral-vibe adapters answer "interactive resume unsupported" and name a manual command instead. `phax artifact decide` resumes its interactive session headless for a structured answer and writes the transcript beside the artifact. It is Claude Code only, because it starts the session with `claude --session-id`, the only way phax can know an interactive session's id in advance. A headless turn (`claude -p`, `codex exec --json`, `vibe -p`) reports its session id in its output stream, on every provider.

Verified on 2026-10-19 with codex-cli 0.153.4:
- A session started by `codex exec --json` resumes in the interactive UI with `codex resume <id>` and shows the headless turn.
- Afterwards, `codex exec resume <id>` sees the interactive turns.
- The whole session is one file, `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*-<id>.jsonl`.
- The first interactive open of a new directory asks the person to trust it, then to review its hooks.

Not verified: whether a `vibe -p` session resumes interactively with `vibe --resume <id>`, because the local install is outdated. Claude Code keeps each session as `~/.claude/projects/<cwd slug>/<id>.jsonl`. Vibe keeps a session directory, which phax already finds to read usage.

Phase sessions run under a security posture:
- Claude Code: its permission flags.
- codex: a `workspace-write` sandbox, with writable roots and network access set.
- vibe: `--workdir` and `--add-dir`, with no per-command or network restriction.

phax already has a read-only mode for Claude Code (its read-only tool set) and for codex (`sandbox_mode="read-only"`). It uses none for vibe. Since Claude Code 2.1.280, a `--resume` invocation reports cost cumulatively over the whole session.

The 2026-10-18 spike showed that the stop by itself is the value. Seeded with the executed phases' handoffs and the upcoming phases' intent, an agent in the stopped worktree saw, unprompted, that "any flaw will spread to all four" later phases. It then turned a review comment into a fix plus a test.
problem:
A plan often has one phase that sets a pattern, such as a record shape, a wording, an error policy or a test style, and later phases that repeat it. Today a person first sees that pattern at the final review. By then it has been copied N times, and they correct it N times. Worse, every later phase read a handoff that described the uncorrected pattern as the one to follow.

A run has no sanctioned place for a person to correct the pattern once, right after the phase that sets it. Stopping a run by hand (interrupt it, edit the worktree, resume) is unsupported. The edits land in the next phase's commit and read as unplanned deviations, no handoff tells the later phases what changed, and nothing turns the correction into a gate that holds them to it.

The first draft of this spec let the person start an optional seeded interactive session. phax could not learn that session's id on codex or vibe, so it could not reuse the session to write the closing handoff and could not capture its transcript. The design worked fully for one provider out of three.

productGoal.statement:
A planner can declare a phase interactive in the plan. When the run reaches that phase, phax sets up its worktree and writes a seed: what to review, the executed phases' handoffs and the upcoming phases' intent. It then runs one headless first turn of the phase's provider, which reads the seed, changes nothing and reports the pattern at stake. phax records that session's id, prints the first reading and the provider's own command to continue the session interactively, stops in `awaiting_review` and exits.

The person corrects the pattern in the worktree, by hand, in the continued session or with any other agent CLI. Where they can, they turn each correction into a guard. `phax resume` runs the gate on the corrected worktree. It gets the interactive handoff by resuming the recorded session headless, or from a fresh session when there is none. It captures the session's transcript into the run folder, commits the phase as the person's and continues. Every later phase reads that handoff, and the gates hold them to its guards.

The plan itself is never rewritten. This is the one sanctioned exception to autonomous runs. It works on every provider phax drives, and every input and output of the stop is a file or a phax command, so a separate review screen can read and write the same files later.
productGoal.guidingRule: A run stops for a person only where its approved plan says so; phax gates, commits and hands off the worktree's diff whatever made it, and every input and output of the stop is a file or a phax command.

terminology.definition: A phase's required `mode` field, placed directly after `optionalFilesToEdit` in a phase of the plan document and of phax-plan.json. Its value is exactly `headless` (an agent session executes the phase, as today) or `interactive` (a person reviews and corrects; the run starts no work session for it).

A phase whose mode is `interactive`. Like any phase, it has its own id, branch, worktree, gate, commit and handoff, and builds on the previous phase. It plans no file to create or edit; its optional files may name what the person is expected to touch. Through those files a bound of assignment-bounds governs it like any phase, and its model and effort are those its first turn and closing turn run. Its Detailed instructions say what to review, which pattern is at stake and which later phases repeat it.
A phase whose mode is `headless`. Every phase that exists today is one.
A choice an executed phase made that later phases are planned to repeat, such as a record shape, a wording, an error policy or a test style.

The file phax writes when a run reaches an interactive phase: `.phax-context/interactive-review.md` in the worktree, with an identical copy, `review-seed.md`, in the phase's run folder. It is never committed.

The one headless turn phax runs at the stop: a new session of the phase's provider, model and effort in the worktree, never a resume of an earlier phase's session. It reads the seed and answers a first-reading document. It must not change the worktree.

The first turn's answer, a versioned `first-reading` document that names the pattern at stake and what each upcoming phase will copy. phax prints it and writes it, rendered, to `first-reading.md` in the phase's run folder.

A session phax started for the interactive phase, by the first turn at the stop or by `phax enter-phase --new-session`, and recorded in `interactive-session.json` with its provider, model, effort, id and start time. The most recent one is the current session.
Whether a provider's own CLI is verified to continue a headless-started session in its interactive UI. The value is exactly `verified` (claude-code, codex) or `unverified` (mistral-vibe).

The provider's own command that continues the current session interactively in the worktree: `claude --resume <id>` or `codex resume <id>`, with the phase's model, effort and posture flags. phax prints it only for a provider whose interactive resume support is `verified`.

The provider's own command that starts a new interactive session in the worktree, with the phase's model and posture flags and an initial prompt pointing at the seed. phax prints it when there is no current session, or when the provider's interactive resume support is `unverified`. phax never learns that session's id.
Whoever works in the interactive phase's worktree. phax knows them only by the git identity of the checkout that closes the phase.
A change in the interactive phase's worktree since the previous phase's commit, made by hand or by any agent. Every file the phase changes is a correction.
A test, lint rule or gate step that fails when a correction is undone or ignored, so that the gates hold the later phases to it.
The interactive phase's handoff, with the sections `## What was corrected`, `## The pattern to follow from now on`, `## Guards` and `## What the next phases need to know`.

The headless turn that writes the interactive handoff at closing. It resumes the current session when there is one and is a new session otherwise. Its answer is a versioned `interactive-handoff` document, and it must not change the worktree.
The run state and phase state of a run stopped at an interactive phase. It is resumable and not a failure, and it is distinct from the run's final `review_open`.
What `phax resume` does to a run in `awaiting_review`. It runs the gate, gets the interactive handoff, captures the transcripts, commits the phase and continues the run.
How an interactive phase closed: `corrected` when the worktree changed, `unchanged` when the person reviewed and changed nothing.
The provider's own record of a recorded session, copied at closing to `interactive-transcripts/<session id>.jsonl` in the phase's run folder.

requirements.title: The per-phase mode
requirements.statement: The system SHALL carry a required `mode` field on every phase of `phax-plan.json` and of the plan document, placed directly after `optionalFilesToEdit`, with a value of exactly `headless` or `interactive`. It SHALL reject a phase that lacks the field or holds any other value.

requirements.title: Reading the mode from plan.md
requirements.statement: WHEN phax parses or extracts a plan.md THE system SHALL give `mode: "interactive"` to each phase whose header paragraph carries the `**Mode:** interactive` line, and `mode: "headless"` to every other phase.

requirements.title: Rendering the mode
requirements.statement: WHEN phax renders a plan document to plan.md THE system SHALL write the `**Mode:** interactive` line in the header paragraph of each interactive phase, after its `**Recommended model:**` and `**Recommended effort:**` lines and, when the phase has one, its `**Assignment reason:**` line. It SHALL write no Mode line on a headless phase.

requirements.title: One lift with assignment-bounds
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax artifact migrate-documents` lifts a live plan sidecar stamped at the 0.25.0 plan-document shape or below THE system SHALL give every phase `mode: "headless"` in the same lift that carries `modelReason` over as `assignmentReason` (assignment-bounds), and SHALL add no Mode line to its plan.md.

requirements.title: Lint: where an interactive phase may sit
requirements.statement: IF an interactive phase is the plan's first phase or its last phase, or directly follows another interactive phase, THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `interactive` check, naming the phase and the rule it breaks.

requirements.title: Lint: an interactive phase plans no work
requirements.statement: IF an interactive phase lists a planned file to create or to edit THEN `phax plans lint` SHALL report an error on the `interactive` check, naming the phase and the file.

requirements.title: An interactive phase is held to the bounds
requirements.statement: The system SHALL hold an interactive phase to the assignment bounds like any phase: its governing bound is the first bound that matches any of its optional files, its model and effort are checked against that bound (or against the policy default when none governs) with its `**Assignment reason:**` line read as for any phase, and its first turn and closing turn run at that model and effort.

requirements.title: One interactive check
requirements.statement: The system SHALL compute the `interactive` findings (where an interactive phase sits and whether it plans work) in one domain check that `phax plans lint` and the run preflight both call, as lint's `models` check and the run's `phase-models` preflight both call `preflightPhaseModels`, so that an error lint reports is the error the run preflight refuses on.

requirements.title: The run preflight refuses an ill-placed interactive phase
requirements.statement: IF the `interactive` check reports an error when `phax run` or `phax resume` runs its preflight THEN the system SHALL refuse before any phase starts (for `phax run`, before the run is named), print every error of the check, each naming its phase, leave an existing run's state unchanged, and exit 11, as the `phase-models` preflight refuses.

requirements.title: The planning skill
requirements.statement: The phax-planning skill SHALL state when to declare an interactive phase: directly after the first phase that sets a pattern at least one later phase repeats, and never by default. It SHALL give the Mode line, and SHALL say that the phase's Detailed instructions name what to review, the pattern at stake and the later phases that repeat it.

requirements.title: Reaching an interactive phase
requirements.statement: WHEN a run reaches an interactive phase THE system SHALL create its worktree on its own phase branch, off the previous phase's branch, and run the project's phase setup commands. It SHALL run no work session, no gate and no fix loop for the phase.

requirements.title: The seed
requirements.statement: WHEN an interactive phase's worktree is set up THE system SHALL write the seed to `.phax-context/interactive-review.md` in the worktree and to `review-seed.md` in the phase's run folder. The seed SHALL hold what is expected of the person (correct the pattern, add guards, keep the scope), the phase's own Detailed instructions, every executed phase's handoff in plan order, the upcoming phases' plan sections, the path of the full plan, the gate commands and the closing command.

requirements.title: The seed is never committed
requirements.statement: The system SHALL never include the seed, `first-reading.md`, `interactive-session.json` or an interactive transcript in any commit of the run's branches.

requirements.title: The first turn
requirements.statement: WHEN the seed is written THE system SHALL run the first turn: a new headless session of the phase's provider, model and effort in the worktree, never a resume of an earlier phase's session. The turn's prompt SHALL ask it to read the seed and answer a versioned `first-reading` document.

requirements.title: The first turn is recorded
requirements.statement: WHEN the first turn returns a valid first-reading document THE system SHALL record the session's provider, model, effort, session id and start time as the current session in `interactive-session.json` in the phase's run folder. It SHALL write the rendered first reading to `first-reading.md` beside that file.

requirements.title: phax's turns run read-only where they can
requirements.statement: The system SHALL run every first turn and every closing turn under the phase's security posture, narrowed to the provider's read-only mode wherever phax has one for that provider: Claude Code's read-only tool set and codex's read-only sandbox.

requirements.title: A first turn that edits is refused
requirements.statement: IF the worktree's tracked files, or its untracked files that are not ignored, differ after a first turn from before it, THEN the system SHALL restore them to their state before the turn, record no session for that turn, and treat the turn as a failed first turn, naming the changed files.

requirements.title: A failed first turn still stops
requirements.statement: IF the first turn fails, through a rate or usage limit, a provider error, or an answer that is still not a valid first-reading document after one corrective resume, THEN the system SHALL still stop at the interactive phase, with no current session. It SHALL name the failure and print the fresh-start command in place of a continue command.

requirements.title: Awaiting review
requirements.statement: WHEN the first turn has ended, whether or not it succeeded, THE system SHALL move the phase and the run to `awaiting_review`, write `resume-instructions.md` for that kind, and release the run lock. It SHALL print the first reading when there is one, the worktree path, the seed path, the continue or fresh-start command, `phax enter-phase` and the closing command, and then exit 13.

requirements.title: No terminal, no wait
requirements.statement: WHILE phax runs without a terminal THE system SHALL stop at an interactive phase exactly as it does with one, and SHALL never read stdin or wait for input there.

requirements.title: The only planned stop
requirements.statement: The system SHALL stop a run to wait for a person only at a phase whose `mode` is `interactive`.

requirements.title: Interactive resume support per provider
requirements.statement: The system SHALL hold each provider's interactive resume support as exactly `verified` or `unverified`: `verified` for claude-code and codex, and `unverified` for mistral-vibe.

requirements.title: The continue command
requirements.statement: WHERE the current session's provider has `verified` interactive resume support THE system SHALL print as the continue command that provider's interactive resume of the current session in the worktree (`claude --resume <id>` or `codex resume <id>`). The command SHALL carry the phase's model and effort and the filesystem and network flags of the phase's security posture.

requirements.title: A provider whose interactive resume is unverified
requirements.statement: WHERE the phase's provider has `unverified` interactive resume support THE system SHALL print the fresh-start command, warn that a session started with it will not be captured, and keep the current session for the closing turn.

requirements.title: Visible as waiting, not failed
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax ls` or `phax session-info` reads a run in `awaiting_review` THE system SHALL show the `awaiting_review` state, the interactive phase and its worktree, distinct from failed and interrupted runs. `phax session-info` SHALL also show the current session, or that there is none. `phax ls --awaiting-review` SHALL list only runs in `awaiting_review`.

requirements.title: The worktree commands target the interactive phase
requirements.statement: WHILE a run is in `awaiting_review` THE system SHALL make `phax path`, `phax shell` and `phax open` target the interactive phase's worktree.

requirements.title: enter-phase continues the session phax started
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax enter-phase <run> <phase>` targets an interactive phase in `awaiting_review` THE system SHALL run the continue command when there is a current session and its provider has `verified` interactive resume support, and the fresh-start command otherwise.

requirements.title: enter-phase resumes codex sessions
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax enter-phase` targets a headless phase whose recorded agent session is a codex session THE system SHALL resume that session interactively with `codex resume <id>` in the phase's worktree, instead of refusing it as unsupported.

requirements.title: --new-session starts another recorded session
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax enter-phase <run> <phase> --new-session` targets an interactive phase in `awaiting_review` THE system SHALL run a new first turn as at the stop and make it the current session, keeping the earlier sessions in the history of `interactive-session.json`. It SHALL then run the continue or fresh-start command.

requirements.title: The worktree diff is the work
requirements.statement: The system SHALL gate, commit and reconcile an interactive phase by its worktree's changes since the previous phase's commit, whatever made them: an editor, a continued session, or an agent phax did not start.

requirements.title: The phase guard holds
requirements.statement: IF `phax resume`, `phax enter-phase` or any other command the phase guard refuses runs inside an interactive phase's worktree THEN the system SHALL refuse it, as for any phase worktree.

requirements.title: Closing runs the gate first
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax resume <run>` targets a run in `awaiting_review` THE system SHALL run the interactive phase's gate on its worktree as it stands, before any agent turn.

requirements.title: A red gate returns the phase to the person
requirements.statement: IF the gate fails while an interactive phase is closing THEN the system SHALL start no fix attempt and no agent turn, keep the attempt's log, commit nothing, leave the phase and the run in `awaiting_review` and exit 4.

requirements.title: The interactive handoff
requirements.statement: The system SHALL accept as an interactive phase's handoff only a document with, in this order, `## What was corrected`, `## The pattern to follow from now on`, `## Guards` and `## What the next phases need to know`. `## Guards` SHALL hold one entry per `## What was corrected` entry, in the same order, each naming a test, lint rule or gate step, or `no guard:` followed by the reason.

requirements.title: A handoff the person wrote takes precedence
requirements.statement: WHERE the person wrote `.phax-context/phase-handoff.md` in the interactive phase's worktree THE system SHALL validate that file as the interactive handoff and use it, running no closing turn.

requirements.title: The closing turn resumes the current session
requirements.statement: WHEN the gate passes on a changed worktree, the person wrote no handoff, and there is a current session, THE system SHALL run the closing turn as a headless resume of that session, given the diff of the corrections. It SHALL ask for a versioned `interactive-handoff` document and render it as the interactive handoff.

requirements.title: A closing turn without a usable session
requirements.statement: IF there is no current session, or resuming it fails for a reason other than a rate or usage limit, THEN the system SHALL run the closing turn as a new headless session of the phase's provider, model and effort, given the seed and the diff of the corrections.

requirements.title: A closing turn that edits is refused
requirements.statement: IF the worktree differs after the closing turn from the gated worktree THEN the system SHALL commit nothing, leave the changes in place, keep the phase and the run in `awaiting_review`, name the changed files and exit 5.

requirements.title: An invalid handoff commits nothing
requirements.statement: IF the handoff fails validation THEN the system SHALL commit nothing, keep the phase and the run in `awaiting_review` and name what is missing or out of place. It SHALL exit 1 when the handoff is a file the person wrote, and exit 5 when it is a closing turn's answer that is still invalid after one corrective resume.

requirements.title: A limit at closing keeps the stop
requirements.statement: IF the closing turn hits a rate or usage limit THEN the system SHALL commit nothing, keep the phase and the run in `awaiting_review`, name the reset time and exit 8.

requirements.title: The transcripts are captured
requirements.statement: WHEN an interactive phase closes THE system SHALL copy each of its recorded sessions from the provider's own session store into `interactive-transcripts/<session id>.jsonl` in the phase's run folder. It SHALL do so after the closing turn, whether or not the person ever continued the session.

requirements.title: A missing transcript never blocks closing
requirements.statement: IF a recorded session's transcript cannot be found or read THEN the system SHALL record it as missing, with the reason, and go on closing the phase.

requirements.title: The phase commit
requirements.statement: WHEN the gate passes and the handoff is valid on a changed worktree THE system SHALL commit the worktree's changes on the phase branch, with the plan's commit subject and body and an `Interactive-Phase: <phase id>` trailer, authored by the checkout's git identity. It SHALL record the phase `committed` with outcome `corrected` and continue with the next phase in the same invocation.

requirements.title: Reviewed without change
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax resume` closes an interactive phase whose worktree has no change THE system SHALL run the gate and use the person's handoff, or else a fixed reviewed-without-change handoff, with no closing turn. It SHALL make an empty commit on the phase branch with the plan's subject and the `Interactive-Phase` trailer and record outcome `unchanged`. It SHALL never treat the phase as having produced no changes (exit 9).

requirements.title: Later phases read the corrections
requirements.statement: WHEN a phase after an interactive phase is dispatched THE system SHALL put the handoff of every earlier interactive phase, in plan order, in a `## Review corrections` section of its prompt. The section SHALL state that it takes precedence over the earlier phases' handoffs where they disagree, and that the phase's own plan section still binds.

requirements.title: The plan is not rewritten
requirements.statement: The system SHALL run the phases after an interactive phase from the plan as it was approved. An interactive phase SHALL change neither the run's `phax-plan.json` nor its plan.md.

requirements.title: Corrections are not deviations
requirements.statement: WHEN phax reconciles the files of an interactive phase THE system SHALL report every file the phase changed as a review correction, and none as an unplanned edit.

requirements.title: The compliance review
requirements.statement: WHEN the compliance review runs on a run with an interactive phase THE system SHALL present that phase to the reviewer as interactive, with its handoff, so that its corrections are judged against that handoff and not as deviations from the plan.

requirements.title: The review handoff and the PR body
requirements.statement: WHEN phax writes `review-handoff.md` or builds the PR body of a run with an interactive phase THE system SHALL show each interactive phase's outcome and committer. `review-handoff.md` SHALL also show its corrections and their guards.

requirements.title: Records
requirements.statement: WHEN records are configured and an interactive phase commits THE system SHALL record its mode, its outcome, its committer, its recorded sessions (provider, model and id) or that there were none, and each transcript's sha256 or that it is missing. WHERE `records.transcript` is true THE system SHALL also record each transcript's content, as it records a phase's `output.jsonl`, under the same destination checks. `phax records explain` on the phase's commit SHALL name them.

requirements.title: The posture is told honestly
requirements.statement: The system SHALL record in an interactive phase's security record that the person's work, including a session they continued, ran outside phax's enforcement. It SHALL also record the applied posture of each first turn and closing turn phax ran.

requirements.title: Cost of phax's turns
requirements.statement: The system SHALL write a cost-ledger entry for each first turn and each closing turn, holding that turn's own cost rather than its session's cumulative cost. It SHALL write none for the turns of a session the person continued, or for a session phax did not start.

requirements.title: Estimating an interactive phase

arbitratedQuestions.question: Does every phase of a plan.md carry a Mode line, or only an interactive one?

options.label: Only an interactive phase carries `**Mode:** interactive`; a phase with no line reads as headless
options.abandons: A one-to-one match between the JSON field and a plan.md line: a headless phase's mode is read from the absence of the line

options.label: Every phase carries `**Mode:** headless` or `**Mode:** interactive`
options.abandons: Every existing plan.md: each one, Approved ones included, fails the structure check until it is edited and re-approved

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: It follows the approved oracle-phases precedent. The persisted formats (phax-plan.json and the plan document) stay explicit and required on every phase. plan.md is an authored grammar, not a persisted schema, so reading absence as headless is not a back-compat shim, and existing plans keep linting.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator (Rémy Loubradou) on 2026-10-20, as recommended, in the joint phase-shape session with assignment-bounds and oracle-phases. Only an interactive phase carries `**Mode:** interactive`, and a phase with no line reads as headless: the persisted formats stay explicit on every phase, and existing plans keep linting. The session also placed the key and the line (J2): `mode` directly after `optionalFilesToEdit` in the plan document and in phax-plan.json, and the Mode line after the Recommended model, Recommended effort and Assignment reason lines. The body revisions for that placement, for the `assignmentReason` rename of assignment-bounds, and for the one plan-document lift this spec shares with it (J5) are recorded under this verdict.
verdict.advocate: Every phase states its mode in plan.md, so the JSON field and the line match one to one and no reader infers `headless` from a missing line.

arbitratedQuestions.question: May an interactive phase also carry planned work?

options.label: No planned file to create or edit; optional files may name what the person is expected to touch
options.abandons: A phase where the person also does work the planner foresaw, such as a guard the planner already knew was needed; that work moves to an ordinary phase before or after

options.label: Planned files are allowed; the person does them along with the review
options.abandons: The file plan as a contract: reconciliation can no longer tell a correction from planned work, and a person who only reviewed leaves the phase's planned files untouched

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Work the planner can foresee belongs to an agent phase, under the gate and the fix loop. The interactive phase exists for what the planner could not foresee. Keeping it review-only is also what lets every changed file count as a correction rather than a deviation.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator (Rémy Loubradou) on 2026-10-20, as recommended, in the joint phase-shape session with assignment-bounds and oracle-phases. An interactive phase plans no file to create or edit, and its optional files may name what the person is expected to touch, so every changed file counts as a correction. The session's other decisions on what an interactive phase carries and where it may sit fit neither question exactly, so their body revisions are recorded under this verdict, the closest: J3, a bound governs an interactive phase through its optional files and its model and effort run the first and closing turns; J4, one `interactive` check called by `phax plans lint` and by the run preflight, which refuses with exit 11 rather than exit 2 (an error lint reports is the error the preflight refuses on; `phax validate --plan` stays a decode); J5, the rule against an interactive phase inside an oracle pair leaves this spec for oracle-phases, re-authored later with its own lift.
verdict.advocate: A person who already knows a guard is needed writes it during the same stop, and the planner need not split foreseeable work into an extra agent phase around the review.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Does a handoff file the person wrote take precedence over the closing turn?

options.label: A valid `.phax-context/phase-handoff.md` is used as written and no closing turn runs
options.abandons: One writer for every interactive handoff: a person's file meets the same validation but gets no agent's help, and its guard list depends on the person's diligence

options.label: The closing turn always writes the handoff; a person's file is passed to it as input
options.abandons: A close with no agent at all: every changed close spends a provider turn, and the person's own words are rewritten by a model before the later phases read them

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The person is the authority on what they corrected. A person who wrote the handoff, or wants no agent involved, should not have their text paraphrased by one. Both paths meet the same validation, so the later phases always read the same shape, and the default close (no file) still costs the person nothing.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, as recommended: a valid handoff the person wrote is used as written, and no closing turn runs.
verdict.advocate: One writer for every handoff: the closing turn always writes it, with the person's file as input.

arbitratedQuestions.question: What does `phax enter-phase --new-session` do at an interactive phase?

options.label: Runs a new headless first turn, records it as the current session, then continues it interactively
options.abandons: A quick fresh start: each new session spends one headless first turn before the person can type

options.label: Only runs the provider's fresh-start command; the closing turn keeps the earlier recorded session
options.abandons: Capture of the new session: phax never learns its id, so the closing turn resumes a session that missed the person's latest work, and the transcript of that work is lost

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Starting headless is the only provider-agnostic way phax learns a session's id, and the id is what lets the closing turn see the person's work and lets phax capture the transcript. A short read-only turn is a small cost next to losing both. A person who wants an uncaptured session can still start one themselves.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, as recommended: --new-session runs a new headless first turn, records it as the current session, then continues it.
verdict.advocate: A quick fresh start that spends no headless turn before the person can type.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Is the review-corrections section marked as taking precedence over earlier handoffs?

options.label: It takes precedence over the earlier phases' handoffs where they disagree; the phase's own plan section still binds
options.abandons: A neutral prompt: phax tells the agent how to weigh its inputs, and a careless correction handoff can override a sound earlier fact

options.label: It is included as one more handoff, with no marking
options.abandons: The point of the stop: the earlier handoffs describe the uncorrected pattern, and an agent that weighs them equally may copy that pattern again

options.label: It also takes precedence over the later phases' plan sections
options.abandons: The decided rule that the approved plan is not rewritten mid-run: a handoff would amend an approved plan without an approval

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The earlier handoffs were written before the correction, and the correction handoff is the only text that knows about both, so it must win where they conflict. The guards back it, so the gate still checks a careless handoff. The plan stays authoritative because it was approved and the handoff was not.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, as recommended: the review-corrections section takes precedence over earlier handoffs where they disagree; the plan still binds.
verdict.advocate: A neutral prompt that does not tell the agent how to weigh its inputs.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Which exit code does `phax run` (or `phax resume`) return when it stops at an interactive phase?

options.label: A new code, 13: awaiting review at an interactive phase (resumable)
options.abandons: Exit 0 for a stop that is not a failure: a shell with `set -e`, or a loop that treats any non-zero code as a failure, must learn 13

options.label: Exit 0
options.abandons: Telling a stop from a finished run by its exit code: a loop such as the steme conductor would read a run waiting for a person as done, and move on to publish or the next plan

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Exits 8 and 9 already make resumable stops non-zero, so a loop's exit-code handling already has the right shape. A loop that mistakes a waiting run for a finished one makes the costlier error: it publishes work the plan said a person must review first.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, as recommended: a stop at an interactive phase exits 13, resumable.

arbitratedQuestions.question: What does an interactive phase reviewed without change leave on its branch?

options.label: An empty commit with the plan's subject and the `Interactive-Phase` trailer
options.abandons: A history without empty commits: a review that changed nothing still adds a commit to the PR

options.label: No commit; the phase branch points at the previous phase's commit
options.abandons: The review as evidence: `phax records explain`, `git log` and the PR show no trace that a person reviewed and confirmed the pattern

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Confirming a pattern is a review outcome worth recording. The commit is where records, attribution and the PR already look, and one empty commit per declared stop is a small cost.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Does the interactive transcript go into the run's records?

options.label: Records carry each recorded session's provider, model, id and the transcript's sha256; the content stays in the run folder
options.abandons: The proof chain's reasoning: a records reader sees that a session took place and can match a kept copy against its digest, but cannot read the conversation behind the corrections

options.label: Records carry the transcript content, under the records transcript setting, like a phase's `output.jsonl`
options.abandons: The person's privacy: their free-form conversation, including anything they pasted, is committed to `phax/records/v1` and travels wherever the records are pushed

options.label: Records carry nothing about the sessions
options.abandons: Any link from the commit to the session that shaped it: `phax records explain` cannot say whether an agent was involved

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Agent transcripts are phax's own output, but an interactive transcript is mostly a person's words, so publishing it should be an explicit choice rather than a side effect of a records setting. The digest keeps the proof chain verifiable against the run folder's copy. The handoff already carries what was corrected and why.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, against the recommendation (digest-only). The interactive transcript is recorded like a phase's output.jsonl: its content goes into the records when `records.transcript` is true, under the same destination checks, and its provider, model, id and sha256 are recorded either way. The reasoning behind the corrections stays readable from the records, and the existing setting, not a new one, decides whether transcripts are published.
verdict.advocate: An interactive transcript is mostly a person's own words, so publishing it should be a choice made for that transcript, not a side effect of the records setting that already publishes agent transcripts.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Are the person's interactive turns in a recorded session counted in the cost ledger from its transcript?

options.label: Never; the ledger counts only the first turn and the closing turn, each by its own increment
options.abandons: Seeing the review's real spend: a long continued session draws on the subscription window with no ledger trace, and window calibration samples that overlap it read high

options.label: Counted as `interactive-turns` entries computed from the copied transcript, and excluded from estimate calibration

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The ledger records what phax ran. The person's continued session is the person's own use of their CLI, like any session outside phax. Parsing unversioned provider transcripts for cost would bring a fragile source into a ledger that `phax plans estimate` relies on. The window calibration already has to tolerate spend outside phax.

verdict.why: Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20, as recommended: the cost ledger counts only the first turn and the closing turn.
verdict.advocate: Seeing the review's real spend in the ledger, computed from the copied transcript.

settled: The stop is declared only in the plan, by the planner, through a required per-phase `mode` enum (`headless | interactive`) in phax-plan.json and in the plan document, placed directly after `optionalFilesToEdit` in both. `mode` is its own key, never a shared `role`. In plan.md only an interactive phase carries `**Mode:** interactive`, after its Recommended model, Recommended effort and Assignment reason lines. It is the one sanctioned exception to autonomous runs, and `phase-decision-requests` stays parked.

Decided by the operator on 2026-10-20 (§9b), in the joint phase-shape session with assignment-bounds and oracle-phases: q-mode-line `interactive-only` (r-mode-parse, r-mode-render) and q-planned-work `review-only` (r-lint-work). The same session settled the phase's shape across the specs: (J1) separate keys, `mode` here and `oracle` in oracle-phases; (J2) `mode` directly after `optionalFilesToEdit`, and the Mode line after the Assignment reason line (r-mode, r-mode-render); (J3) a bound governs an interactive phase through its optional files, and that phase's model and effort run its first and closing turns (r-bounds); (J4) one `interactive` check, called by `phax plans lint` and by the run preflight, which refuses with exit 11 (r-interactive-shared, r-refuse); (J5) oracle-phases does not ride this release's lift.

This spec and assignment-bounds ship together, with one frozen copy of the 0.25.0 plan-document shape and one lift by `phax artifact migrate-documents`, which renames `modelReason` to `assignmentReason` and gives every phase `mode: "headless"` (r-mode-lift). `assignmentReason`, `model` and `effort` stay the phase's last three keys.

`phax validate --plan` stays a decode of `phax-plan.json`: it rejects a missing or unknown `mode`, and runs neither the `interactive` check nor any other preflight, as it runs no `phase-models` check today.

The rule that an interactive phase may not sit strictly between an oracle phase and the phase that discharges it is no longer this spec's. oracle-phases, reopened to Draft on 2026-10-20, carries it when it is re-authored (on `gate-report`, after `steme oracles` exists, with its own plan-document lift), together with which commit the discharge judges after a person's correction.
An interactive phase is a phase of its own: id, branch, worktree, setup, gate, commit and handoff, building on the previous phase. It runs no work session and no fix loop.

At the stop, phax runs one headless first turn of the phase's provider, model and effort: a new session, read-only where the provider allows, with any edit refused by comparing the worktree before and after the turn. phax records the session's id, prints the first reading and the provider's own continue command, and exits 13 in `awaiting_review`. A failed first turn still stops, with the fresh-start command instead.

Interactive resume support is an explicit per-provider value: `verified` for claude-code and codex (codex verified on 2026-10-19 with codex-cli 0.153.4), `unverified` for mistral-vibe. For an unverified provider phax prints a fresh-start command, and only that session's transcript is lost. The codex session adapter's interactive resume is lifted for every phase.
The person works with any editor and any agent CLI. phax gates, commits and reconciles the worktree's diff whatever made it.

Closing is `phax resume <run>` from the main checkout, and the phase guard still refuses it inside the worktree. The order is gate first, then the handoff (the person's file, else a closing turn resuming the current session, else a fresh session), then transcript capture, then the commit, then the next phase in the same invocation. A red gate, an edit by the closing turn, an invalid handoff or a limit all leave the phase in `awaiting_review` and commit nothing.

The interactive handoff has its own four sections, with one guard (or `no guard:` and a reason) per correction. Every later phase reads it in a `## Review corrections` prompt section, not only the next phase.
The approved plan is never rewritten mid-run, and `adjust-plan --landed` refuses a run awaiting review.

`mode` also changes `phax-plan.json`, a second persisted format, and the extraction cache entry that embeds its schema. How cache entries and in-flight runs written by an older binary are treated is left to planning; plan sidecars are lifted by the lift shared with assignment-bounds.

Explicit per-variant enums: `mode` is `headless | interactive`, the outcome is `corrected | unchanged`, interactive resume support is `verified | unverified`, the first-turn outcome is `answered | failed | refused-change`, and the guard kind is `test | lint | gate-step | none`. `awaiting_review` is a new run state and a new phase state, never `interrupted` with a free-text reason.

State transitions go only through `src/domain/state.ts` and the reducer that interprets events against PhaxState. The new transitions are: running → awaiting_review at the stop; awaiting_review → running on closing; back to awaiting_review on a red gate, an editing closing turn, an invalid handoff or a limit; and awaiting_review → archived with --force. A reset follows today's reset-phase rules.
Every provider answer carries a required `$schema`, and an answer with none, or of an unknown version, is refused.

Respect the layers. The seed, the worktree comparison verdict, the handoff validation and the prompt section are pure domain or app logic, and every file write, git operation, provider spawn and session-store read goes through its port.

The phax CLI gains no network access. The first turn and the closing turn are provider sessions spawned through the Backend port, as every phase's are. The continued session is the provider's own CLI, which phax only prints or execs.

Provider-agnostic: nothing may depend on a Claude Code feature the other providers lack. Learning a session's id comes from the headless turn's stream, never from `--session-id`, and a read-only mode is a narrowing used where it exists, never the only guard.
The cost ledger takes each resumed turn's own increment, never a session's cumulative cost (Claude Code 2.1.280 and later report cumulative cost on `--resume`).
The phase guard's classification is unchanged: resume, enter-phase, shell and open stay refused inside a phase worktree.
